title: Gallo pinto
desc: Breakfast, and there is no other option

sn.e: It is early.
It is not hot yet.

sn.s: Doña Carmen está en la cocina.
sn.e: Doña Carmen is in the kitchen.

sn.s: De la cocina viene un olor rico.
sn.e: A good smell comes from the kitchen.
"Buenas, doña Carmen," I say.
"Buenas. Come and eat," she says.
"I am not hungry," I say.
Doña Carmen does not hear me.
Or does not want to hear me.

sn.s: Pone un plato en la mesa.
sn.e: She puts a plate on the table.

sn.s: En el plato hay arroz con frijoles.
sn.e: On the plate there is rice with beans.

sn.s: El arroz y los frijoles están juntos.
sn.e: The rice and the beans are together.
"This is called gallo pinto," she says.
"Gallo pinto?" I ask.
"Gallo pinto. Rice and beans."

sn.s: El gallo pinto se come en la mañana.
sn.e: Gallo pinto is eaten in the morning.

sn.s: El gallo pinto lleva arroz y frijoles.
sn.e: Gallo pinto has rice and beans in it.

sn.s: Los frijoles son rojos y pequeños.
sn.e: The beans are red and small.

sn.s: Sin frijoles no hay gallo pinto.
sn.e: Without beans there is no gallo pinto.

sn.s: Doña Carmen cocina los frijoles en la cocina.
sn.e: Doña Carmen cooks the beans in the kitchen.

sn.s: En la cocina hay una olla grande de frijoles.
sn.e: In the kitchen there is a big pot of beans.

sn.s: En la cocina huele a café.
sn.e: The kitchen smells of coffee.

sn.s: El café se toma dulce aquí.
sn.e: Coffee is drunk sweet here.

sn.s: Tomo el café y como la tortilla.
sn.e: I drink the coffee and eat the tortilla.

sn.s: Comer en la mañana es importante.
sn.e: Eating in the morning is important.
Here people eat early.

sn.s: Se come en la casa, no en la calle.
sn.e: People eat at home, not in the street.
Eating alone is a strange thing here.
And they eat a lot.

sn.s: Doña Carmen pone otro plato en la mesa.
sn.e: Doña Carmen puts another plate on the table.
That plate is for Roberto.

sn.s: Al lado del gallo pinto hay una tortilla.
sn.e: Next to the gallo pinto there is a tortilla.

sn.s: La tortilla es gruesa y está caliente.
sn.e: The tortilla is thick and hot.
There is cuajada too.

sn.s: La cuajada es blanca y salada.
sn.e: Cuajada is white and salty.

sn.s: Y hay café en un vaso.
sn.e: And there is coffee in a glass.
The coffee is very sweet.
Doña Carmen sits down.

sn.s: Roberto también se sienta a comer.
sn.e: Roberto sits down to eat too.
Roberto eats fast.
Doña Carmen eats little.

sn.s: Ella prefiere ver comer a los demás.
sn.e: She would rather watch other people eat.
I eat slowly.
The gallo pinto is good.
It is really good.
"Do you like it?" doña Carmen asks.
"I like it a lot," I say.
"It is very good," I say.
Doña Carmen smiles.

sn.s: Pone más gallo pinto en mi plato.
sn.e: She puts more gallo pinto on my plate.
"Doña Carmen, no more," I say.

sn.s: Ella pone más de todos modos.
sn.e: She puts more on anyway.
"Eat," she says. "You're thin."

sn.s: Roberto se ríe con la boca llena.
sn.e: Roberto laughs with his mouth full.
"My mum always says that," he says.
I eat all the gallo pinto.
I eat all the tortilla.
I drink all the coffee.
"And what do we eat tomorrow?" I ask.
Roberto gives me a strange look.
"Gallo pinto," he says.
"And the day after?" I ask.
"Gallo pinto," Roberto says.
"Always gallo pinto?"

sn.s: "Siempre", dice doña Carmen desde la cocina.
sn.e: "Always," doña Carmen says from the kitchen.
"In the morning, gallo pinto."

sn.s: "Y a veces en la noche también."
sn.e: "And sometimes at night as well."

sn.s: Pienso que eso va a ser mucho arroz.
sn.e: I think that is going to be a lot of rice.
A lot of rice and a lot of beans.
But I say nothing.
The gallo pinto is good.

sn.s: Doña Carmen me da otra tortilla.
sn.e: Doña Carmen gives me another tortilla.
"For the road," she says.
"Thank you, doña Carmen."
"You're welcome, mijo," she says.

sn.s: Es la primera vez que me dice mijo.
sn.e: It is the first time she calls me mijo.

sn.s: Roberto me explica en la calle.
sn.e: Roberto explains it to me in the street.
"Mijo is like son," he says.

sn.s: "Mi mamá le dice mijo a todos."
sn.e: "My mum calls everyone mijo."

sn.s: Pero yo llegué hace tres días.
sn.e: But I arrived three days ago.

sn.s: Y ya como en su cocina.
sn.e: And I already eat in her kitchen.
And she already calls me mijo.

sn.s: Aquí la comida es una puerta.
sn.e: Here food is a door.

sn.s: Uno come y ya está adentro.
sn.e: You eat and you are inside.
